answer: One concrete defense ties each agent standing to a scarce, non-cloneable deposit that is slow to rebuild. Picture reputation as a vine that only climbs after months rooted in a single identity: fork yourself into a thousand Sybils and each shoot starts bare at the knoll base. Because trust is mined like shale, extracted slowly layer by layer from honest countersigned work, spinning up fakes costs far more than they can ever earn back, so the attack simply never pays for itself.
